---
title: "How to write your own lfpack file"
---

`compress_bin_to_h5` starts from a SpikeGLX binary. For anything else (another acquisition
system, simulated data, an array already in memory) use `compress_to_h5`, which runs only the
codec on a time-first `(ns, nc)` float32 `.npy`:

```python
import numpy as np
from lfpack import compress_to_h5

np.save("probe00.npy", data)   # (ns, nc) float32, already at the rate to store
compress_to_h5("probe00.npy", "session.lf.h5", recording="probe00", fs=250.0, alpha=7.0)
```

`recording` is any unique key (IBL uses the probe-insertion UUID); it becomes the top-level
HDF5 group and is what `LFPackReader(..., recording=)` selects. Pass `h=` for the probe
geometry and `channels=` for brain locations; see
[`compress_to_h5`](../reference/compress_to_h5.qmd) for every parameter.

## Several recordings in one file

Write one file per recording, then merge them without re-compressing:

```python
from lfpack import merge_h5, subset_h5

merge_h5(["probe00.lf.h5", "probe01.lf.h5"], "session.lf.h5")
subset_h5("session.lf.h5", "probe01_only.lf.h5", recordings=["probe01"])
```

## Attach sync {#sync}

**Affine**: a sync-corrected rate and start time, enough for ordinary clock drift:

```python
compress_to_h5("probe00.npy", "probe00.lf.h5", recording="probe00", fs=250.0,
               t0_sync=12.345, fs_sync=249.998)
```

**Piecewise**: when the sample-to-time mapping is not a straight line (a step, a truncated
recording), write the knots after compression. `write_sync_attrs` also stores their
least-squares affine as `t0_sync`/`fs_sync`, and the reader interpolates through the knots:

```python
import h5py
import lfpack

with h5py.File("probe00.lf.h5", "a") as f:
    meta = f["probe00/00/meta"]
    lfpack.clear_sync_attrs(meta)                           # drop a previous attempt
    lfpack.write_sync_attrs(meta, sample_knots, time_knots)  # float64, increasing
```
